Solid arrows indicate logical implications, while dashed arrows indicate conceptual dependencies. The layout highlights the progression from the definition of the circular foliation map to its asymptotic and geometric consequences.

nodes.name: \rm\bf Theorem 1.4: G _G _G is a chart of
nodes.statement:
The Teichm\"uller space \(\mathcal{T} (S,\underline{p})\) is a manifold of real dimension \(6g-6+3n\).
For each triangulation \(G\in\text{Tri}(S,\underline{p})\), let \(\mathcal{T}(G)\subset \mathcal{T} (S,\underline{p})\) be the locus where \(G\) admits a geodesic realization.
Then the circular foliation map
\[
\mathcal{C}_G:\mathcal{T}(G)\longrightarrow \mathcal{MF} (S,\underline{p})
\]
is a homeomorphism.
Moreover, the family \(\{(\mathcal{T}(G),\mathcal{C}_G)\}_{G\in\text{Tri}(S,\underline{p})}\) provides an atlas of \(\mathcal{T} (S,\underline{p})\) modelled on the common space \(\mathcal{MF} (S,\underline{p})\cong \mathbb{R}^{6g-6+3n}\).

nodes.name: \rm\bf Definition 5.18: Circular foliation map _G
nodes.statement:
For \(G \in \text{Tri}(S,\underline{p})\), the {\em circular foliation map}
\[
\mathcal{C}_G : \mathcal{T}(G) \longrightarrow \mathcal{MF} (S,\underline{p})
\]
is defined as the composition
\[
\mathcal{C}_G := (i^{(G)}_{\cdot})^{-1} \circ \ell^{(G)}_{\cdot},
\]
where \(\ell^{(G)}_{\cdot}\) is the edge length map and
\((i^{(G)}_{\cdot})^{-1}\) is the inverse edge intersection map.

nodes.name: \rm\bf Corollary 1.8: _G _ u t S
nodes.statement:
For each triangulation \(G \in \text{Tri}(S,\underline{p})\), the map
\[
  \mathcal{C}_{G} : \mathcal{T}_{\rm u.t.}(S,\underline{p}) \longrightarrow \mathcal{MF} (S,\underline{p})
\]
is an embedding.

nodes.name: \rm\bf Corollary 1.5: Shear--radius on G
nodes.statement:
For each triangulation \(G \in \text{Tri}(S,\underline{p})\), the map
\[
  \mathcal{SR}_G : \mathcal{T}(G) \longrightarrow \Lambda_G
\]
is a homeomorphism onto the vertex-balanced cone \(\Lambda_G\).

nodes.name: \rm\bf Proposition 5.17: Edge parametrizations are homeomorphisms
nodes.statement:
For each \(G \in \text{Tri}(S,\underline{p})\), both the edge intersection map
\(i^{(G)}_{\cdot}\) (Definition~3.3)
\[
i^{(G)}_{\cdot} : \mathcal{MF} (S,\underline{p}) \longrightarrow \Omega_G
\]
and the edge length map \(\ell^{(G)}_{\cdot}\) (Definition~4.10)
\[
\ell^{(G)}_{\cdot}: \mathcal{T}(G) \longrightarrow \Omega_G
\]
are homeomorphisms.

nodes.name: \rm\bf Theorem 1.3: Shear--radius on
nodes.statement:
For each triangulation \(G \in \text{Tri}(S,\underline{p})\), the shear--radius map
\[
  \mathbf{sr}_G : \mathcal{MF} (S,\underline{p}) \longrightarrow \Lambda_G
\]
is a homeomorphism onto the vertex-balanced cone \(\Lambda_G\).
In particular, shear and radius parameters provide a global coordinate system on \(\mathcal{MF} (S,\underline{p})\).

nodes.name: \rm\bf Theorem 1.6, \rm\bf Theorem 1.7: Asymptotic limits
nodes.statement:
For each \(G \in \text{Tri}(S,\underline{p})\) and each \(X_0 \in \mathcal{T}(G)\), the peripheral stretch ray \((X_t)_{t \ge 0}\) based at \(X_0\) converges, in the simple-curve length-spectrum topology, to the hyperbolic surface with cusps at \(\underline{p}\) which is described by the shear coordinates of \(X_0\).

For each \(G \in \text{Tri}(S,\underline{p})\) and each \(X_0 \in \mathcal{T}(G)\), the interior anti-stretch ray \((X_t)_{t \le 0}\) based at \(X_0\) converges, in \(\mathcal{T}(G)\), to the hyperbolic circle-packed cone-surface with centers at \(\underline{p}\) which is described by the radius coordinates of \(X_0\).

nodes.name: \rm\bf Definition 6.2: Partial stretch / anti-stretch
nodes.statement:
For a given triangulation $G \in \text{Tri}(S,\underline{p})$, we define two one-parameter families of deformations on the space $\mathcal{T}(G)$, called {\em partial (anti-)stretch deformations}. 
Both are obtained by pulling back the corresponding scaling actions on $\mathcal{MF} (S,\underline{p})$ via the circular foliation map $\mathcal{C}_G$:
\[
 \xymatrix{
  \mathcal{T}(G) \ar[d]_{\mathcal{C}_G} \ar[r]^{{\rm stretch}_G^{\cdot}} & \mathcal{T}(G) \ar[d]^{\mathcal{C}_G}  \\
  \mathcal{MF} (S,\underline{p}) \ar[r]^{{\rm exp}_{\cdot}(t)} &  \mathcal{MF} (S,\underline{p}) .
 }
\]

\begin{itemize}
    \item The {\em peripheral (anti-)stretch deformation} is the map
    \[
      {\rm stretch}^{\mathrm{per}}_G : \mathcal{T}(G) \times \mathbb{R} \longrightarrow \mathcal{T}(G),\qquad
      {\rm stretch}^{\mathrm{per}}_G(X,t) := \mathcal{C}_G^{-1} \circ {\rm exp}_{\mathrm{per}}(t) \circ \mathcal{C}_G(X).
    \]
    
    \item The {\em interior (anti-)stretch deformation} is the map
    \[
      {\rm stretch}^{\mathrm{int}}_G : \mathcal{T}(G) \times \mathbb{R} \longrightarrow \mathcal{T}(G),\qquad
      {\rm stretch}^{\mathrm{int}}_G(X,t) := \mathcal{C}_G^{-1} \circ {\rm exp}_{\mathrm{int}}(t) \circ \mathcal{C}_G(X).
    \]
\end{itemize}
For both types of deformation, the case $t > 0$ is called a {\em stretch}, and the case $t < 0$ is called an {\em anti-stretch}.

nodes.name: \rm\bf Proposition 7.2, \rm\bf Theorem 1.10: Max cone angle in G _ u t S
nodes.statement:
Let \(G\in\text{Tri}(S,\underline{p})\) be a triangulation and \(p\in\underline{p}\) a marked point.
Then
\[
\theta_p(G)=\pi\,|F_p(G)|,
\]
where \(|F_p(G)|\) is the number of faces of \(G\) incident to \(p\).

The following statements hold:
\begin{enumerate}
  \item If \(n = g = 1\), then \(\Theta(S,\underline{p}) = 2\pi\) and \(\mathcal{T} (S,\underline{p}) = \mathcal{T}_{\rm u.t.}(S,\underline{p})\).  Otherwise, \(\Theta(S,\underline{p}) = \pi\).
  \item The value \(\Theta(S,\underline{p})\) cannot be achieved by any element of \(\mathcal{T}_{\rm u.t.}(S,\underline{p})\), except in the case \(n = 1\) and \(g \ge 2\).
\end{enumerate}
